standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: lemma-separable-degree ([L : K]_s = |Mor_K(L, K-bar)|), lemma-characterize-normal (normality via equal images of embeddings, and its converse), uniqueness of the normal closure (lemma-normal-closure); standard fact: a K-subalgebra of an algebraic closure is a field (domains algebraic over a field are fields)
core_obligations: Set n = [L : K]_s = |Mor_K(L, K-bar)| = {sigma_1, ..., sigma_n} and let M' be the K-subalgebra of K-bar generated by sigma_1(L), ..., sigma_n(L); M' is a field

Any K-algebra map M' -> K-bar permutes the sigma_i (tau composed with sigma_i is again a K-embedding of L), so sends M' into and onto M'; by lemma-characterize-normal M' is normal over K and is the smallest normal subextension of K-bar containing sigma_1(L); by uniqueness of normal closure M is isomorphic to M'

The multilinear map lambda_1 (x) ... (x) lambda_n -> sigma_1(lambda_1) ... sigma_n(lambda_n) is a surjective map of K-algebras from the n-fold tensor power onto M' (its image generates M'), and n <= [L : K] by definition of the separable degree
proof_roadmap: Build M' from the conjugate embeddings and identify it as a field
Prove normality and minimality through the permutation of embeddings
